provenance: Positives are retracted papers named by Crossref's own retraction NOTICES (update-to); the detector reads the PAPER's updated-by. Two separately deposited fields, so this measures whether the back-link is populated rather than re-reading our own input. Negatives are works with no update of any kind.

limits.what_this_measures: MECHANISM recall: given a DOI that Crossref knows is retracted, does the pipeline read the back-link and say so. It does NOT measure how often a submission cites a retracted paper — that base rate is low (order of one finding per few hundred submissions), and this check is taken for the single-instance reputational cost of publishing on a retracted source, not for recall.
limits.cache_delay: CACHE_TTL_MS.found is 30 days, so a paper retracted AFTER we cached it goes unflagged for up to 30 days. Accepted: retraction is permanent once it happens, so the check is late, never wrong.
limits.coverage: DOI-only by construction. arXiv identifiers short-circuit past Crossref, and DataCite carries no equivalent field — both record retracted:null, which means NOT CHECKED rather than clean.
limits.expression_of_concern_excluded: 269 works carry one. An open investigation is not a withdrawal, and telling an author their source was retracted when it was not is the worst output this pipeline can produce.

what_the_plan_got_wrong.wrong_field: The plan said read `update-to`. That lives on the retraction NOTICE and points back at the paper. The paper carries `updated-by`. Reading update-to would have flagged nothing on any real submission — 0% recall, silently, since a check that never fires is indistinguishable from a clean corpus.
what_the_plan_got_wrong.wrong_filter: The plan said filter to source === 'retraction-watch'. Measured here: 91 of 150 real retractions were deposited by `publisher`. That filter alone would have cut recall from 100% to ~39%.
